items.summary:
Semyon Varlamov waited long enough.

items.body: Teammates, coaches thrilled for goalie, who calls it 'very special moment' Nearly two years since previously winning an NHL game, the 38-year-old goalie was mobbed by his New York Islanders teammates after their 4-3 shootout victory at the Nashville Predators on Tuesday, a celebration honoring Varlamov's long journey back to the League following double partial knee replacements. It was Varlamov's first win since Nov. 14, 2024, when he made 24 saves in a 5-2 victory at the Vancouver Canucks. It's been so long, only seven skaters from that night were in the lineup in Nashville. But after the medical marvel proved to Islanders brass in training camp he was physically able to return to the NHL, Varlamov went his first three starts this season without a win, going 0-1-2. "It's an amazing feeling, a very special moment," Varlamov told reporters after the game, following his 20-save performance. "A year ago, to be honest with you, I didn't see this coming. It was such a grind, like the last two years, to get to this point when you have the opportunity to play and then compete at the highest level in the world. I mean, I'm very thankful for this opportunity." Perhaps it was fitting Barry Trotz was on hand at Bridgestone Arena, the former Islanders coach now a senior adviser with the Predators, the team he coached from its inception in 1998 until leaving for the Washington Capitals in 2014. He won his first Stanley Cup championship four years later before helping turn the Islanders around during a four-season run (2018-22) that was highlighted by back-to-back trips to the third round of the Stanley Cup Playoffs. items.summary: Kaprizov’s incredible chance generation is nearly at the same level as his insane goal total.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Mandatory Credit: Matt Blewett-Imagn Images Very rarely does a superstar player’s stat line cause a double take. After all, these players are the best of the best. We should be accustomed to seeing them put up crazy numbers every season. Heck, Connor McDavid is averaging almost three points a game, and no one is batting an eye because it’s not out of the realm of possibility for a player of his caliber. But Kirill Kaprizov’s start to the season might raise an eyebrow or two. If you told me that, one eighth into the season, he’d be leading the league in goal scoring, I wouldn’t be surprised. He’s an incredibly talented player, and he’s playing alongside Matt Boldy and Quinn Hughes. That’s a recipe for success, so an increase in goal scoring isn’t all that surprising. But 14 goals in 14 games is a stat line that raises a few more questions. First off, it’s very rare for a player to average a goal per game in the NHL, at least since the league’s early years. According to NHL.com, only 31 players have averaged a goal-per-game pace or higher in a season with a minimum of 18 games played (the fewest games ever played in an NHL regular season, occurring in 1918-19). Twenty-four of those instances happened in the first seven seasons of the league, when teams consistently averaged four-plus goals per game. items.body: The record-breaking save came at 17:45 of the third period in St. Louis on Tuesday, Montreal Canadiens goalie Jacob Fowler turning aside the 12-foot snap off the stick of Blues forward Connor McMichael. It was the 42nd of 46 saves that Fowler would make, his airtight goaltending in Montreal's 2-0 victory, giving him the Canadiens record for most saves in a game by a rookie. In so doing, he anchored his team's third straight victory on its four-game road trip, which concludes against the Dallas Stars at American Airlines Center on Thursday (8 p.m. ET, Prime Video, TSN2, RDS). Technically, Esposito wasn't yet a rookie, winning the Calder Trophy with the 1969-70 Chicago Black Hawks. items.title: Oilers place Zach Hyman on injured reserve
items.summary: Hyman has one goal in six games with the Oilers in 2026-27. He has already missed six games due to injury.
items.body: Hyman, 34, left Monday’s game against the Detroit Red Wings in the second period after he took a hit from Red Wings’ defenseman Andreas Englund. He appeared to hit his head against the glass and fell to the ice, then required help to the dressing room from the Oilers’ training staff. He finished the night with two shots on goal in 8:25 of ice time. Hyman’s injury comes soon after he missed more than two weeks due to an injury sustained during Edmonton’s regular-season opener against the Vancouver Canucks on Sept. 29. He missed six games then returned to the lineup Oct. 17 against the Utah Mammoth . Through six games, Hyman has one goal and is averaging 17:56 of ice time. Now in his 12th NHL season, the Toronto native has 262 goals and 234 assists for 496 points in 717 regular-season games with the Oilers and Toronto Maple Leafs . He scored a career-high 54 goals with Edmonton in 2023-24. Hyman, a 2010 fifth-round pick for the Florida Panthers , also has 42 goals and 33 assists for 75 points in 106 career Stanley Cup Playoff games. He was part of the Oilers’ back-to-back Stanley Cup Final runs in 2024 and 2025, and scored a league-leading 16 goals during the postseason in 2024. Edmonton is 8-2-2 with 18 points through their first 12 games of 2026-27. Connor McDavid, Leon Draisaitl and Evan Bouchard make up three of the NHL’s top-five point leaders going into Wednesday night, with McDavid having 34 in just 12 games.

items.summary: Zach Hyman is heading back to the injured reserve.
items.body: The Edmonton Oilers forward has been placed on IR with a "stiff neck," head coach Mike Babcock told reporters on Wednesday. Hyman suffered the injury in Monday's loss to the Detroit Red Wings when he took a hit from Andreas Englund. He hit his head hard on the glass and appeared dazed. He required assistance to leave the ice. Hyman was in just his fifth game back after missing over two weeks with an upper-body injury he suffered in the Oilers' pre-season finale. Despite the pre-season injury, Hyman did play in the regular-season opener before going on IR. The 34-year-old has one goal in six games played this season.

items.title: Charlie Jacobs to take over from father as Bruins’ governor
items.summary: Charlie takes the reins from his dad, Jeremy, continuing the family legacy that spans over a half-century.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: David Kirouac-Imagn Images A huge change in operations in New England. On Wednesday, the Boston Bruins announced that CEO Charlie Jacobs is going to take over as the team’s governor from his father, Jeremy M. Jacobs, who held the role for 51 years. Charlie will represent the club on the NHL’s Board of Governors. “It is a tremendous honor to step into the role as governor of the Boston Bruins,” the younger Jacobs said in a release. “Representing the team that has been part of my family for the past 51 years. I step into this role with the goal of continuing to build upon the incredible legacy and the impact that my dad has had on this franchise and the NHL over his five decades of leadership. Dad will continue to serve as my mentor and sounding board through this next era of the Bruins. I am looking forward to partnering with the NHL Board of Governors Chairman Ted Leonsis, Vice Chair Murray Edwards, our peers, and Commissioner Bettman on continuing to grow this beautiful game that we all love.” The move to promote Charlie comes as Jeremy is starting to move out of the spotlight. Last month, he stepped down as Chairman of the league’s board of governors, and Washington Capitals owner Ted Leonsis was unanimously voted in as the new chair. Charlie has been part of the organization since 2000, when he was named the Bruins’ alternate governor. He also serves as the CEO of Delaware North, a multinational food service and hospitality company, which has ownership shares of NESN, the Bruins’ local broadcaster.

items.body: Hockey Hall of Famer, New Jersey exec thrilled to land goalie in trade with Jets Martin Brodeur believed the New Jersey Devils reached the point where a move for an elite goaltender like Connor Hellebuyck wasn't just warranted. It was necessary. New Jersey's core players are entering or firmly established in the prime of their careers. Brodeur, its executive vice president of hockey operations, said acquiring the 33-year-old goalie reflects the Devils' commitment to take the next step. "It's like the window of winning," Brodeur said in an interview with NHL Network on Tuesday. "Our guys are there. You look at Nico Hischier (27 years old), Jack Hughes (25), Jesper Bratt (28), Timo Meier (30), they're (mostly) all in their late 20s, with Jack a little younger. But I think it was time for us to make a move like that. (General manager) Sunny (Mehta) pulled it off, and it's awesome." Brodeur understands perhaps better than anyone what Hellebuyck provides -- a proven No. 1 goalie who embraces the responsibility that comes with being one of the most important players on the team. Hellebuyck made 17 saves Tuesday for his first victory with New Jersey, a 5-1 win at the Dallas Stars in his first NHL game since April 13, four days after being acquired in a trade with the Winnipeg Jets for forwards Dawson Mercer and Nick Bjugstad , goalie Nico Daws , the rights to unsigned draft choice Alexander Command , the Devils' own second-round pick in the 2029 NHL Draft and their seventh-round selection in the 2027 NHL Draft. items.body: Out of the NHL most of last season, the veteran bench boss, in a supporting role on Canada's staff for the league's return to Olympic hockey, was tasked with a large chunk of the scouting work. An 18-year-old defenceman turning heads early in his professional career forced himself into the conversation. Matthew Schaefer was ultimately left off the roster that settled for a gut-wrenching silver medal at February's Milan Cortina Games. DeBoer, however, would still get a chance to work alongside the blue-line phenom after being hired by the New York Islanders with four games left in the 2025-26 campaign. "What a privilege to coach a player like that," DeBoer, who's with his sixth NHL organization, said recently. "He's even better live and in-person than he is on tape … a real difference-making player. There are very few of them in the world, and he's one. The No. 1 pick at the 2025 draft, Schaefer swept the Professional Hockey Writers Association's 198 ballots to capture the Calder Trophy as rookie of the year in May — the first unanimous winner since Teemu Selanne in 1992-93 — after putting up 59 points in 82 games. Schaefer became the first defenceman in more than nine decades to lead all rookies (outright or tied) in goals with 23. items.body: Register Login Flames, Morgan Frost Begin Extension Talks By Ethan Hetu | at October 28, 2026 9:30 am Among all of the free agents the Calgary Flames currently have on their roster, none is more important than center Morgan Frost . The 27-year-old is Calgary’s No. 2 center, and there is a strong argument to be made that Frost is the team’s most skilled offensive pivot by a wide margin. But with the Flames engaged in a full-scale rebuild, it’s fair to wonder whether the Flames will be best served signing Frost to an extension versus exchanging him for a collection of draft picks and prospects. As of now, it seems the Flames will at least make a real effort to extend Frost before considering a trade. Yesterday, on TSN’s Insider Trading segment , Pierre LeBrun reported that Flames GM Craig Conroy had an initial meeting with Frost’s agent, Darren Ferris of Quartexx, to “get the ball rolling” on negotiations of a contract extension for Frost. LeBrun also noted that while Ferris has a reputation for wanting to bring his clients to the open market in order to maximize their earning potential, in this case, there is “mutual interest” in finding a deal to keep Frost in Calgary and away from free agency. A 2017 first-round pick, Frost has long been a player whose true value has been difficult to nail down. He’s a skilled offense-first pivot who scored a career-high 19 goals and 46 points with the Philadelphia Flyers, but also struggled to break through as a true top-six talent. Frost’s inability to develop beyond middle-six status, combined with his proclivity for inconsistent play, led the Flyers to trade him to the Flames in a January 2025 deal that included Joel Farabee and Andrei Kuzmenko . items.title: When star goalies get traded in their primes: A case study
items.summary: Connor Hellebuyck wasn’t the only superstar stopper to change teams in the past 25 years.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Congratulations to Connor Hellebuyck. After a public trade request and holdout, the star goaltender finally escaped the wintry wasteland of Winnipeg to reach the sunny climes of… Newark, New Jersey? OK, Hellebuyck’s move from the Winnipeg Jets to the New Jersey Devils may not have gotten him the palm trees and tax breaks that have been so en vogue for NHL players lately, but the 33-year old might just be the final piece for a talented young team that has been trying to get over the proverbial hump for years now. Will the deal put the Devils over the top? Will it help nourish a successful new era for the Jets? Well, there’s already been sharp analysis on the trade as we still sit in its aftershock, but truly, none of us can see the future, and only time will give us a definitive answer. In the meantime, maybe the best we can do, as a wise mandrill once said, is learn from the past. So, to map out the possible outcomes of this Jets-Devils deal, let’s look back at six times since over the past 25 years that an established, star-level goalie of Hellebuyck’s stature was traded in his prime. The Deal: Buffalo sent Miller, along with forward Steve Ott, to St. Louis in exchange for goaltender Jaroslav Halak, forwards Chris Stewart and William Carrier, a first-round pick, and a third-round pick. Why did it happen?: Miller was still playing at an elite level entering the 2013-24 season, but the Sabres had missed the playoffs in each of the previous two years and were seemingly headed in a direction that would be of no interest to a 33-year-old goaltender. The team made the most significant trade of last season when they acquired Quinn Hughes from the Vancouver Canucks, and beyond that, the club has been engaged in a longstanding search for a true No. 1 center. A KHL champion with the ability to play both at center and on the wing, Yurov scored 12 goals and 27 points in 73 games in 2025-26, his rookie KHL campaign. items.title: Red Wings’ Michael Brandsegg-Nygård has emerged as a serious Calder Trophy threat
items.summary: The numbers are good, the eye test is great – the hype is legit for the 21-year-old Norwegian.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect When the Detroit Red Wings drafted Michael Brandsegg-Nygård 15th overall in 2024, they knew they were getting a near-NHL-ready winger. His two-way game was mature, his hockey sense was solid, and he knew how to wire a shot better than most his age. But did anyone expect him to play at more than a 50-point pace in his first NHL campaign? The Norwegian superstar is off to an incredible start in Detroit. He had one point in 14 games with the big club a year ago, but he primarily played with the AHL’s Grand Rapids Griffins, where he had 20 goals and 44 points. But this year, the numbers have been much better than expected. The 2026 IIHF World Championship bronze medalist is up to eight points through 12 games, highlighted by a trio of multi-point outings. He failed to get on the scoresheet in three of the past four games, but he’s still tracking for 56 points this year. MBN has blown expectations out of the water already. And here’s the thing: his game isn’t about driving offense. Sure, Brandsegg-Nygård is capable of creating quality chances, but he’s much more dangerous away from the puck. For starters, he’s hitting everyone in sight. Kiefer Sherwood set the all-time single-season hits record back in 2024-25 with 462. Yakov Trenin moved into second with 413 last year in Minnesota. Right now, Brandsegg-Nygård is tracking for 378 over the full season – that would put him fourth behind Jeremy Lauzon (383 in 2023-24). There’s still plenty of time for Brandsegg-Nygård to have his point production fall a bit, but he could be the only player of the bunch to get more than 370 hits and 45 points in a season. items.title: Canucks Takeaways: Lekkerimaki leads third-period comeback to end skid
items.summary: Thanks to an OT snipe from Filip Hronek and some late-game heroics from Jonathan Lekkerimaki, the Canucks finally found some good vibes. Courtney Jacobsen has the takeaways from Tuesday’s slump-busting win.
items.body: In the midst of a prolonged losing streak, the Vancouver Canucks were in desperate need of some good vibes. With just one win in the month of October, it was getting understandably difficult for the Canucks to maintain some positivity about what they're building towards. And when Quinn Hughes and the Minnesota Wild handed the Canucks their 10th straight loss Sunday, morale was at an all-time low. But Tuesday night against the Anaheim Ducks, the Canucks clawed back from an early deficit, earning an impressive 6-5 victory to get finally back into the win column thanks to an overtime snipe from Filip Hronek and some late-game heroics from Jonathan Lekkerimaki. It was a win that took a fair bit of resilience from a dejected Vancouver squad. For much of the night in Southern California, the Canucks looked to be headed to a familiar fate. A three-goal second period from the Ducks put the Canucks into a 4-1 hole that seemed, at times, insurmountable. But goals from Brock Boeser and Jamie Oleksiak in the early goings of the third cut into the Ducks' lead, perfectly setting the stage for Lekkerimaki to score twice with the net empty to force overtime. It was the sixth time in franchise history that the Canucks rallied from a three-goal, third-period deficit. "It was a big win for us," Lekkerimaki told reporters post-game, who gave all the credit to Jake DeBrusk for screening Ducks goalie Lukas Dostal on both his goals. "We have to build on it." It would be an understatement to say that it's been a trying season for the Canucks, where moral (and real) victories have been few and far between through 14 games. items.title: Canucks rally to beat Ducks in OT, snap 10-game losing streak
items.body: ANAHEIM, Calif. — Filip Hronek scored a power-play goal with 11 seconds to go in overtime to cap a run of four consecutive goals by the Vancouver Canucks , who snapped a 10-game losing streak with a 6-5 comeback win over the Anaheim Ducks on Tuesday night. The Canucks, who won for just the third time all season, trailed 5-2 after Anaheim's A.J. Greer scored his second goal of the game with 7:37 to play in regulation. But Jamie Oleksiak pulled Vancouver within 5-3 just 31 seconds later. Jonathan Lekkerimaki then scored twice less than a minute apart — the second with 1:57 left in regulation — to send the game into overtime. In addition to his winning goal, Hronek also had an assist. Liam Ohgren and Brock Boeser also had goals for Vancouver, while Elias Pettersson added a pair of assists. Leevi Merilainen made 18 saves. The Ducks jumped to a 4-1 lead after two periods. Greer scored in the first period, then Jeff Malott, Beckett Sennecke and Leo Carlsson added second-period goals. Sennecke's came on the power play. Jackson LaCombe had three assists for the Ducks and Lukas Dostal made 27 saves.

items.title: Senators begin five-game road trip with loss to Golden Knights
items.body: LAS VEGAS — Raphael Lavoie scored his first career goal, a tap-in eight minutes into the third period to put Vegas ahead for good in its 4-1 victory over the Ottawa Senators on Tuesday night, ending the Golden Knights' three-game losing streak. Braeden Bowman scored a power-play goal for the Golden Knights, and William Karlsson and Jack Eichel each added an empty-netter. Nic Dowd got his 200th career point with a secondary assist on Lavoie's goal. Adin Hill stopped 25 shots, including a daring charge out of the net. Fellow goalie Carter Hart did not play after sustaining an undisclosed injury during the morning skate. Shane Pinto scored on a power play for the Senators, who opened a five-game trip. Jonas Johansson made 25 saves. The Golden Knights got on the scoreboard late in the second period thanks to a tremendous defensive play from Hill. Ottawa's Ridly Greig had a short-handed breakaway opportunity, but Hill raced out of his net to the right circle to poke away the puck. Vegas quickly got the puck to the other end, and Bowman deposited a rebound off Ivan Barbashev's shot from the right circle with 11 seconds left in the period. Ottawa answered just 34 seconds into the third when Drake Batherson made a terrific pass to Pinto in the slot for the tying goal. That was Batherson's eighth point in five games, and it's the sixth game in a row the Golden Knights have allowed a power-play goal. Lavoie, playing in his 27th game, then put Vegas back on top with his goal after a pass from Ville Heinola.

items.title: Fowler cementing place as Canadiens starter with another win
items.summary: After a 46-save shutout against the Blues, goaltender Jacob Fowler is making it impossible for the Canadiens to turn away from him, writes Eric Engels.
items.body: Jacob Fowler pushed to his right, stopped a shot from Jake Neighbours, and then quickly scrambled to his left and sprawled to take a sure goal away from Dylan Holloway. It was his last save of the night, a 10-beller if we’ve ever seen one, and we’re not even sure it was the best of the 46 he made to preserve a 2-0 shutout for the Montreal Canadiens over the St. Louis Blues. We can’t say how this game might have turned out with Jakub Dobes in Montreal’s net. In St. Louis, a city in which Dobes spent his teenage years as a USHLer, he might’ve been just as brilliant. But Martin St. Louis elected not to start Dobes and had to be elated he instead stuck with the hot hand — and not just after watching Fowler stuff Holloway on the doorstep of his crease with 1:12 remaining in a game the 21-year-old had already dominated. Fowler was the story of Sunday’s Heritage Classic; the big-game goalie shining on the biggest and brightest stage , taking yet another giant leap on his rapid ascent up the NHL ladder and cementing his place as Montreal’s starter. He made 33 saves on 34 Winnipeg Jets shots for his fifth straight win just two nights after stopping 20 of 21 against the Chicago Blackhawks for his fourth. On Monday, Fowler was named the league’s third star of the week for those performances. On Tuesday, he deserved all three stars against the Blues, even if he twice told reporters in the visitors' room at Enterprise Center he “just got lucky.” One shot from Neighbours hit the post early in the game, and that was fortunate for Fowler. But the puck hit him 46 times, and there was nothing lucky about it. items.summary: DALLAS -- Connor Hellebuyck’s tenure with the New Jersey Devils began on a high note.
items.body: Goalie allows just one goal in win against red-hot Stars, was 'making plays everywhere' DALLAS -- Connor Hellebuyck ’s tenure with the New Jersey Devils began on a high note. The 33-year-old goaltender made 17 saves for his new team in a 5-1 victory against the Dallas Stars at American Airlines Center on Tuesday. The start came less than a week since the three-time Vezina Trophy winner was acquired by New Jersey in a trade with the Winnipeg Jets on Friday for forwards Dawson Mercer and Nick Bjugstad , goalie Nico Daws , the rights to forward Alexander Command , a second-round pick in the 2029 NHL Draft and a seventh-round pick in the 2027 NHL Draft. When asked what was going through his head during the national anthem, Hellebuyck answered with a single word: “Finally.” It makes sense, considering the trade for Hellebuyck came on the day his suspension, which began on Sept. 16, was scheduled to come to an end. As a result of the impasse with Winnipeg, Tuesday was also his season debut. Not that you would have known it by watching Hellebuyck play. “If you asked me, I was ready two months ago,” he said. “I just had the mindset since the day I got here that I want to get in.” And he made an impact right away, according to Devils captain Nico Hischier . “He came in and was making plays everywhere,” Hischier said. “He just spread this calmness out. items.title: Islanders’ Schaefer becomes first player post-lockout to play all five minutes of overtime
items.summary: The 19-year-old defenseman finished the game with over 32 minutes of ice time.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images New York Islanders defenseman Matthew Schaefer exceeded all expectations in his rookie campaign last season. Now, just a dozen games into his sophomore season, he’s done something we haven’t seen in over 20 years. In New York’s 4-3 shootout win over the Nashville Predators on Tuesday, Schaefer became the first player since the 2004-05 lockout to play all five minutes of overtime. Schaefer drew a tripping penalty on Predators forward Filip Forsberg 2 minutes and 17 seconds into the overtime period, giving him a chance to grab a breather during a stoppage in what is typically relentless 3-on-3 action. Of course, the Islanders kept Schaefer out there for the entirety of the proceeding 4-on-3 power play, and he stayed on for the remaining 43 seconds after the power play had ended to complete the full five minutes of OT. The 19-year-old blueliner even had to get on his horse to impede a potential breakaway for Forsberg after he stepped out of the penalty box. The Hamilton, Ontario native finished the game with 32 minutes and 16 seconds of ice time, clearing the next closest Islanders skater by over six minutes. Coming into Tuesday’s game, he was averaging 26 minutes and 13 seconds of ice time. Schaefer also notched an assist on Tuesday, giving him two goals and nine assists for 11 points in 12 games this season. Last season, he put up 23 goals and 36 assists for 59 points in all 82 games en route to winning the Calder Trophy as the league’s top rookie. New York, now sitting in fourth place in the Metropolitan Division with 14 points through 12 games, will finish up a three-game road trip against the Minnesota Wild on Thursday before kicking off a three-game homestand against the Edmonton Oilers on Saturday.

items.title: Schaefer plays all five minutes in OT as Islanders beat Predators
items.summary: Matthew Schaefer continues to raise the bar in his second NHL season.
items.body: Matthew Schaefer continues to raise the bar in his second NHL season. The 19-year-old defenceman played all five minutes in overtime as the New York Islanders won 4-3 in a shootout over the Nashville Predators . Schaefer is the first player to not take a shift off in an overtime period since the NHL began tracking that data in 2009-10. He finished the game with 32:16 of ice time, the third most by any player in a game this season, and picked up an assist. The reigning Calder Trophy winner has once again anchored the Islanders through the first month of the season. He now has 11 points in 12 games while averaging 26:43 of ice time, fourth most league-wide. The assist extended his personal point streak to five games. Kyle Palmieri and Bo Horvat scored in the shootout as the Islanders salvaged a win after letting an early lead slip away. Horvat, Anthony Duclair and Brayden Schenn had staked the Islanders to a 3-0 lead in regulation but the Predators forced overtime with goals from Filip Forsberg, Alexander Kerfoot and Ryan O'Reilly. Semyon Varlamov got the win for the Islanders, his first win in nearly two years.

items.title: Kapanen picking up speed with some of NHL’s fastest skating for Oilers
items.summary: EDMONTON -- Kasperi Kapanen can fly and has the numbers to prove it.
items.body: Fourth in NHL in bursts over 22 mph, including highest maximum by a forward EDMONTON -- Kasperi Kapanen can fly and has the numbers to prove it. The Edmonton Oilers right wing posted the fastest maximum skating speed of any NHL forward this season at 24.05 miles per hour in a 3-1 win at the San Jose Sharks on Oct. 10, per NHL EDGE stats . Only St. Louis Blues defenseman Philip Broberg has clocked faster with a burst of 24.26 mph in a 5-2 loss at the Nashville Predators on Oct. 17. “If I’m up there, that means I’m still a decent skater,” Kapanen said Tuesday. “Skating has always, since I started playing hockey, something that I was good at. I was always one of the fastest ones out there. But even though it is your strength, I love working at it as well and trying to be better.” Kapanen will get another chance to display his speed when the Oilers host the Calgary Flames at Rogers Place on Wednesday (8:30 p.m. ET; Prime). Kapanen’s top speed this season is the fastest by an NHL forward since Nathan MacKinnon of the Colorado Avalanche topped out at 24.78 mph in a 3-2 loss against the Blues on April 5 last season. Kapanen has nine bursts over 22 mph this season, which is tied with New York Islanders defenseman Matthew Schaefer for fourth, behind teammate Connor McDavid (26), MacKinnon (24) and Toronto Maple Leafs forward Jack Roslovic (10). “Playing with guys like ‘Davo’ (McDavid) it does inspire me in a way to work on my skating,” Kapanen said. “I know I’m never going to keep up with him, but you can try and learn things, so it’s always going to be a big factor for me.” McDavid is considered one of the fastest skaters in NHL history, and he doesn’t slow down all that much when he has the puck. items.body: ST. LOUIS — Jacob Fowler made a career-high 46 saves for his second shutout of the season, and Zachary Bolduc and Florian Xhekaj scored as the Montreal Canadiens defeated the St. Louis Blues 2-0 on Tuesday night. Mike Matheson had two assists as the Canadiens (7-3-2) improved to 4-1-1 on the road this season with their third straight away victory. Fowler’s shutout was his third in 24 career starts. The Blues (5-6-1) fell to 3-2-1 at home as they were shut out for the second straight game. They lost 4-0 to visiting Carolina on Saturday. Bolduc put the Canadiens ahead with 11:23 left in the second period, slapping a one-timer from the right circle for his fifth goal of the season. Bolduc’s first goal against his former team was assisted by Matheson and Alexandre Texier. A first-round draft pick in 2021 by St. Louis, Bolduc scored 19 goals for the Blues during the 2024-25 season before being traded to the Canadiens for defenseman Logan Mailloux. The 23-year-old right winger had 12 goals and 30 points for Montreal in 78 games last season. Xhekaj scored the first goal of his NHL career with 17:43 remaining in the third period off a redirection of a shot by Matheson. Xhekaj’s goal, in his ninth game, was assisted by Matheson and Kirby Dach.

items.title: Stars’ Kyle Capobianco exits game vs. Devils with lower-body injury
items.summary: The Stars struggled in a blowout loss to the Devils and also lost a depth defenseman in the defeat.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Dallas Stars fell in a 5-1 home blowout to the New Jersey Devils on Tuesday night as Connor Hellebuyck made his debut for the visitors, but the night got worse in the final frame for the home team. After struggling to find consistency, the Stars had to play the final minutes without defenseman Kyle Capobianco in the lineup. The 29-year-old was forced to leave the game after limping off the ice with an apparent leg injury after suffering a hit from Devils forward Timo Meier. While Capocianco remains a depth piece for head coach Glen Gulutzan’s Stars, the injury bug has not been kind to the team this season. items.body: PHILADELPHIA — Kent Johnson scored his second goal of the game 2:22 into overtime and the Columbus Blue Jackets beat the Philadelphia Flyers 4-3 on Tuesday night after coughing up a three-goal lead. Columbus scored three goals in a 2:46 span of the first period to lead 3-0 after one. Johnson set up Adam Fantilli for the first goal at 10:58 of the first period, and then deflected Zach Werenski's shot past Flyers goalie Dan Vladar at 12:54. Denton Mateychuk scored for Columbus 50 seconds later. Cam Talbot made 28 saves for his third win this season. Johnson scored the overtime winner on a two-on-none breakaway, following a give-and-go with Fantilli. It was Johnson's sixth goal of the season. Philadelphia forced overtime by outshooting Columbus 28-6 over the final two periods. Noah Cates scored his first goal of the season by poking a loose puck past Talbot, while Trevor Zegras cut the deficit to 3-2 with just under five minutes left in regulation. Zegras slid a pass to Tyson Foerster, who fired a shot on Talbot that Jamie Drysdale tipped into the net with 11 seconds remaining. Despite losing consecutive games, the Flyers have scored points in four of five games after starting the season with a franchise-record nine-game winless streak. Columbus won consecutive games for the first time this season. Blue Jackets: Continue their road trip in Carolina on Thursday. Flyers: Travel to Washington to play the Capitals on Wednesday.

Lacroix began his NHL career with the Flyers in 1967-68 and played 245 games with them over four seasons. The center led Philadelphia in points twice, finishing with 56 points (24 goals, 32 assists) in 75 games in 1968-69, and 58 points (22 goals, 36 assists) in 74 games in 1969-70. Lacroix then was traded to the Chicago Black Hawks for 1971-72 before joining the WHA with the Philadelphia Blazers the following season, when he led the league with 124 points (50 goals, 74 assists). He also played for the New York Golden Blades/Jersey Knights, San Diego Mariners, Houston Aeros and New England Whalers over his seven WHA seasons. In 1974-75, his first season with San Diego, Lacroix won his second WHA scoring title with 147 points (41 goals, 106 assists) in 78 games. He also set the professional record for assists that season; at the time, he was the only player other than Bobby Orr (102 assists for the Boston Bruins in 1970-71) who had ever reached 100 in a single season of professional hockey. The record stood until Wayne Gretzky had 109 assists for the Edmonton Oilers in 1980-81. Lacroix is the WHA all-time leader in points (798, including 251 goals), assists (547) and games played (551). Following the WHA-NHL merger in 1979, Lacroix returned to the NHL for a sixth and final season, playing for the Hartford Whalers in 1979-80 before retiring. items.body: LAS VEGAS — Vegas Golden Knights goalie Carter Hart left the team's morning skate with an undisclosed injury, and Adin Hill will start Tuesday night's game against the Ottawa Senators. “He's in good hands,” coach Ryan Craig said. “We've got a plan here moving forward either way. We'll be ready for tonight.” Hart is 4-3-1, with a 2.76 goals-against average and an .889 save percentage, but he has shared much of the net time with Hill (4-1, 2.95, .882). Both goaltenders have dealt with injuries over the past several seasons. Hart missed nearly three months last season after injuring his left leg and then was expected to back up Hill in the playoffs. But then-coach Bruce Cassidy was fired with eight games left, and replacement John Tortorella instead put Hart in the net. Hart delivered by helping lead a late surge in the regular season before going 12-4 over the first three rounds with a 2.22 GAA and .924 save percentage. He struggled in the Stanley Cup Final against Carolina, however, becoming the first goalie to allow at least four goals in the first five games. The Hurricanes won the series in six games. Hart's presence in Vegas was a controversial topic in the hockey world and beyond. He was one of five players from the 2018 Canada world junior team who were acquitted last July of sexual assault. The NHL ruled those players were eligible to sign deals beginning Oct. 15, 2025, and to play starting Dec. 1. Hart signed a two-year, $4 million contract with the Golden Knights.

items.body: Register Login Blue Jackets Activate Dante Fabbro By Brennan McClain | at October 27, 2026 2:31 pm According to a team announcement , the Columbus Blue Jackets activated defenseman Dante Fabbro from the injured reserve. Columbus had an open roster spot, so they didn’t need to make a corresponding roster move. Fabbro, 28, has been recovering from a broken hand suffered in preseason. The right-handed blueliner will return after missing the first four weeks of the regular season and the Blue Jackets’ first nine games of the 2026-27 campaign. Based on line rushes from practice, Fabbro will play on Columbus’ bottom pairing next to Erik Gudbranson . Fabbro will begin his ninth NHL season and second full season with the Blue Jackets. Columbus claimed Fabbro off waivers from the Nashville Predators around this time a few years ago. The early stages of his tenure with the Blue Jackets were promising. Fabbro typically played with Zach Werenski , allowing him to score nine goals and 26 points in 62 games with a +23 rating, averaging 21:39 of ice time per game. He also earned a 91.7% on-ice SV% at even strength, one of his career-best marks. Given his chemistry with Werenski, Columbus quickly signed Fabbro to a four-year, $16.5MM ($4.125MM AAV) extension. Unfortunately, he didn’t play as well last season. Fabbro finished the 2025-26 campaign with five goals and 11 points in 74 games with a -16 rating, averaging 16:34 of ice time per game. He continued to block shots at a high rate, but nearly every offensive and defensive metric fell. Regardless, the Blue Jackets continue to inch toward a healthy defensive corps. After activating Fabbro, defenseman Ivan Provorov is the only defenseman left on the injured reserve as he continues to recover from a lower-body injury.

Through the first month of the year, the Bruins have massively exceeded those expectations. On Tuesday night, they will take on the reigning Stanley Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes in a showdown between the teams with the two best records in the league, but it’s the Bruins and not the Hurricanes who own the NHL’s best record by points percentage with a record of 9-2-1. items.title: Kindel practices with Penguins, wants to ‘move forward’ following health scare
items.summary: CRANBERRY, Pa. -- Ben Kindel practiced with the Pittsburgh Penguins on Tuesday for the first time since losing consciousness while aboard the team plane one week ago.
items.body: Forward could return Thursday after losing consciousness on team plane last week CRANBERRY, Pa. -- Ben Kindel practiced with the Pittsburgh Penguins on Tuesday for the first time since losing consciousness while aboard the team plane one week ago. The 19-year-old forward took full contact during a session that lasted more than an hour. He has missed two games since Oct. 20, when he experienced a vasovagal syncope, a common cause of fainting that occurs when a sudden drop in heart rate and blood pressure results in reduced blood blow to the brain. "Felt pretty good," Kindel said. "Was nice to be back out there with the guys and preparing for this weekend. ... I wouldn't say it's that tough. For me, it's in the past now. It's out of my head. Can't control what happened. Just have to move forward. "That's where my head's at. Just looking to move forward now. So, I'm definitely not dwelling on anything or have anything holding me back coming into this weekend." One day after playing 18:53 in a 5-4 loss at the Utah Mammoth on Oct. 19, Kindel fell unconscious for about 10 minutes shortly after the plane departed Salt Lake City International Airport. He received oxygen before an emergency medical landing and was transported to the University of Utah Hospital. Kindel said he began working out one or two days after collapsing. "Obviously, an interesting experience," Kindel said. "I think the Penguins kind of explained it pretty good in their releases and (general manager Kyle Dubas') press conference and everything. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images The highly anticipated New Jersey Devils debut for one of the more successful netminders of this generation is here. It’ll be interesting to see what the Devils get from the three-time Vezina Trophy winner. While Hellebuyck is undoubtedly accomplished and talented, he hasn’t seen any game action this year. He also only just practiced with the Devils on Monday, his first on-ice session with a team this year, as he was suspended by Winnipeg after failing to report to training camp last month. Yet optimism in the Garden State runs high, as many believe Hellebuyck’s addition makes the Devils a certified favorite in the Metropolitan Division. Oct. 20th: The Calgary Flames have recalled a forward after placing Samuel Honzek on the injured reserve yesterday. According to a team announcement , the Flames recalled Ben Jones from the AHL’s Calgary Wranglers. Although Jones replaces Honzek on the Flames’ active roster, he won’t replace him in the lineup. Instead, Jones is taking the spot of captain Mikael Backlund . According to TSN’s Pat Steinberg , Backlund is day-to-day with an upper-body injury after leaving Calgary’s recent contest against the Carolina Hurricanes with a few minutes left in the third period. The Flames are sending a message by recalling Jones. He may not be a prized prospect, or even the most skilled, but Calgary is showing that those who play the best in the AHL will get the first nod should an opportunity arise. Make no bones about it, Jones has been the Wranglers’ best player early in the 2026-27 campaign. In seven games, the 27-year-old forward has scored seven goals and two assists. The team’s next closest goal-scorers are Sam Morton and Rory Kerins with three each. Unfortunately for Jones, there’s no guarantee he plays. Despite Backlund’s upper-body injury, he hasn’t officially been ruled out for Thursday’s contest against the Minnesota Wild. Jones was centering the team’s top line this morning, meaning he very well could be a placeholder in practice and will quickly come out of the lineup if Backlund is healthy.

items.title: Why are hockey players the only athletes chasing small markets?
items.summary: Hellebuyck was the latest example of a star player being willing to join a team outside of the big city.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Ed Mulholland-Imagn Images In the fallout from Connor Hellebuyck being traded to the New Jersey Devils , one thing has become clear: NHLers are happy going to teams outside of the big cities. The Devils acquired the Hart Trophy winner from the Winnipeg Jets , another notable small market in the NHL, last week. It led many to believe hockey players seek markets where they won’t be recognized and are willing to move outside Canada. However, that might just be the way hockey players are built compared to athletes from the other three major sports in North America. On Monday’s edition of Daily Faceoff LIVE , Colby Cohen joined Tyler Yaremchuk and Carter Hutton to discuss why hockey players seem to be the only ones who desire to play in smaller markets. Most of these guys, they don’t necessarily want to be the center of attention wherever they go. They don’t need to be the center of attention in a restaurant. They don’t need to be the center of attention in a grocery store. Most guys, and I feel very comfortable saying this, will stop. Will give time. Will be that guy at the rink that takes pictures with all the kids, right? But they want to do it, and they don’t need to be noticed, and they don’t need to be celebrated for it. items.title: ‘I put him in a tough spot’: Rangers coach on James Reimer’s tough debut
items.summary: Reimer gave up three goals on eight shots in just one period Monday against the Kings.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect James Reimer made his New York Rangers debut Monday night against the Los Angeles Kings , but he was pulled after he gave up three goals on eight shots in the opening frame. The Rangers lost 6-3, and head coach Mike Sullivan pointed the blame at himself in the post-game media availability. “For (Reimer) to come in the way he has, in short order, and to go into a game like this. It’s not an easy challenge. It’s a tough challenge. I just felt the game was going, I just felt like maybe (Reimer) needs a little more preparation before we put him in that circumstance,” he said. It’s been a whirlwind two weeks for Reimer. He was signed to a professional tryout with the Hartford Wolf Pack , the Rangers’ AHL affiliate; became the oldest AHL goalie to record a shutout in nearly 20 years, then signed a one-year contract with the Rangers on Sunday. New York needed a goaltender after former Vezina Trophy winner Igor Shesterkin suffered a season-ending injury earlier this month. Including Monday’s game, Reimer has a 232-191-67 record with a .909 save percentage (SV%) and 2.88 goals against average (GAA) in 540 career games with the Rangers, Ottawa Senators , Anaheim Ducks , Buffalo Sabres , San Jose Sharks , Carolina Hurricanes , Florida Panthers and Toronto Maple Leafs . Reimer, a native of Morweena, Man., is 5-5 with a .925 SV% and 2.70 GAA in 11 career Stanley Cup Playoff games. He led the Leafs through seven games in a first-round, seven-game series against the Boston Bruins in 2013. New York is 7-6-1 with 15 points through their first 14 games of 2026-27. items.body: EDMONTON — If you came away with anything from the Edmonton Oilers ’ 4-3 shootout loss to the Detroit Red Wings Monday night, it was that the young guys looked pretty good. The only problem was, the young guy who looked the best was 24-year-old Michal Postava, the goaltender making his first National Hockey League start in the Red Wings’ net. “He’s solid,” said Ryan Nugent-Hopkins , the third Oiler to be thwarted by Postava in the shootout, allowing Lucas Raymond’s wrist shot past Tristan Jarry to stand up as the game-winner. “I thought he was good positionally and always there. items.body: Toronto Maple Leafs captain Auston Matthews is pushing back on the third-period penalty called against him in Monday's loss to the Calgary Flames. Matthews was called for delay-of-game midway through the final frame with his Maple Leafs trailing by one goal — the seventh penalty assessed to Toronto and negating a power play that had only just begun for the Maple Leafs. On-ice officials determined that the 29-year-old played the puck with his glove following a faceoff, which results in a delay-of-game penalty per NHL Rule 67.2. "I think you've got to be sure 100 per cent," he said to reporters after the game in Calgary. "I fall. I don't even know what exactly the rule is, if you have to cover it or whatever, but I've got a lot of respect for the refs. They're going to make what they feel is the right call. They're not perfect, but obviously in that situation, I feel like you really gotta be sure." Matthews said he wasn't given an explanation after his penalty. The official rule states that a player shall be assessed a minor penalty if he attempts to win a face-off by batting the puck with his hands. The two players involved in the actual face-off (the centres) are not permitted to play the puck with their hand without incurring a penalty under this rule until such time as a third player (from either team) has at least touched the puck. Once the face-off is deemed complete (and a winner of the face-off is clear) hand passes shall be enforced as per Rule 79 – Hand Pass. With an assist on William Nylander's third-period goal on Monday, the captain became the fastest player in franchise history to reach the 800-point milestone, doing so in just 703 games. He surpassed previous record-holder Darryl Sittler, who hit 800 in 742 games in 1980. The 2022 league MVP is off to another hot start, with nine goals and 11 assists in 14 games. Matthews has produced at a point-per-game clip in all but two seasons in his 10-year career. items.body: NEW YORK — Drew Doughty had a goal and two assists, and Artemi Panarin added a power-play goal and an assist as the Los Angeles Kings beat the New York Rangers 6-3 on Monday night. The Kings won for the third time in their last four games — all on the road — after going winless over their first six games of the season. Los Angeles jumped on New York early, chasing goaltender James Reimer after one period. Reimer was pulled in his Rangers debut after allowing three goals on eight shots. Reimer played just one previous game this fall, a 35-save shutout in the American Hockey League on Saturday night, before signing an NHL contract for the rest of the season. Taylor Ward opened the scoring 1:15 into the game on the Kings’ first shot. Brandt Clarke made it 2-0 at 4:52 of the first, tipping in a rebound off Joel Armia's slap shot. J.T. Miller got New York on the board when a Tye Kartye slap shot deflected off his skate and past Darcy Kuemper. Mikey Anderson and Taylor Ward added second-period goals for the Kings before Adam Fox cut the deficit to 5-2 on the power play with 6:55 to play in the second. Kartye got the Rangers within two at 16:08 of the third period, before Joel Edmundson scored in an empty net for his first goal of the season for Los Angeles. Kuemper made 23 saves to pick up his third win of the season. After replacing Reimer, Dylan Garand stopped 15 of the 17 shots he faced. A moment of silence was held prior to puck drop for 1970s and ’80s Rangers fan favourite Ron Duguay, who died last week.

NHL Monday Night Hockey complements the already established NHL Saturday and NHL Sunday presented by Fastenal European primetime games and creates a unique weekday matinee experience for fans in North America. items.title: Jets get welcome distraction from Heritage Classic, look for on-ice reset
items.summary: Winnipeg’s Heritage Classic delivered a much-needed celebration of the franchise’s history and following Connor Hellebuyck’s departure, the Jets look to turn the page and put the focus on turning things around on the ice.
items.body: By almost every account, the NHL's Heritage Classic festivities were a smashing success. The Jets couldn't quite tie the bow on the weekend, falling 2-1 to the Montreal Canadiens in front of a sold-out crowd at Princess Auto Stadium. But everything from the fan festival to a heavy dose of nostalgia at the alumni game, to the marquee event on a beautifully sunny Sunday was executed with passion and style, generating incredible energy from start to finish. "Myself personally, I told my grandkids to be ready for the (military) flyover (before the game) and I'm sure that's all they're going to talk about is the jets and the helicopters," head coach Scott Arniel said of the atmosphere. "To be in a Canadian market, two Canadian teams like that, that's special." Jets captain Adam Lowry was equally appreciative of the moment, both for Winnipeg and the greater hockey community. "It was a spectacular spectacle," Lowry said. "It takes you back to youth hockey, it takes you back to growing up when you fell in love with the game." Beneath all the cheers and nostalgia, however, the Heritage Classic served as the perfect distraction from the circus that had been playing out in Winnipeg ever since franchise goaltender Connor Hellebuyck publicly demanded a trade in August.
